message.content: The last common ancestor of lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) was a small, omnivorous mammal that lived roughly 60–70 million years ago. It belonged to the clade **Laurasiatheria**, the group that gave rise to the separate lineages that eventually became the families Felidae (cats) and Equidae (horses). No specific species name is known for this ancestor; it is simply the most recent common ancestor of the two lineages.

The common ancestor would be a mammal from the order Artiodactyla? Wait, lion is a carnivore, zebra is an equid. They belong to different orders: Carnivora vs Perissodactyla. The common ancestor would be a mammal from the clade Laurasiatheria? Actually, both belong to the clade Laurasiatheria. The common ancestor would be a mammal from the clade Eutheria (placental mammals). But maybe they want the last common ancestor of the two species: the last common ancestor of the family Felidae and Equidae. That would be a mammal from the clade Laurasiatheria, likely a member of the clade Panarthropoda? No.

We can answer: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras was a placental mammal that lived around 60-70 million years ago, belonging to the clade Laurasiatheria. It would have been a small, omnivorous mammal that gave rise to the separate lineages that eventually became the families Felidae (cats) and Equidae (horses). So the common ancestor is a mammal from the clade Laurasiatheria, likely a member of the group called "Artiodactyla"? Wait, no, Artiodactyla includes even-toed ungulates like deer, pigs, cows. Equids are perissodactyls. So the common ancestor is a mammal from the clade Laurasiatheria, but not necessarily a specific species. So we can say: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras was a small, omnivorous mammal that lived about 60-70 million years ago, belonging to the clade Laurasiatheria. It is not known as a specific species, but it would have been a member of the group that gave rise to the carnivores and perissodactyls. So the answer: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras was a small, omnivorous mammal that lived around 60-70 million years ago, belonging to the clade Laurasiatheria. Or we can mention that the common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae is a mammal from the clade Laurasiatheria, likely a member of the group called "Artiodactyla"? Wait, no.

Thus answer: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras was a small, omnivorous mammal that lived around 60-70 million years ago, belonging to the clade Laurasiatheria. It is not known as a specific species.
